videos.title: The Gestalt Principles for User Interface Design
videos.why: A quick overview of how grouping principles decide which elements people see as one unit and which as separate; watch it first, then the proximity video.

videos.title: Proximity: Gestalt Principle for User Interface Design
videos.why: Shows how spacing alone tells people which items belong together and which play different roles; it is the same effect the lab-gestalt sliders let you try by hand.

podcasts.episode: Follow These Principles of Gestalt for Better UX Designs (feat. Erin Malone)
podcasts.why: Erin Malone talks through her short chapter on Gestalt for UX practitioners; a compact audio recap of the principles in this lesson for a walk or commute.

reads.title: Proximity Principle in Visual Design
reads.why: The most useful Gestalt principle for interfaces, with examples from text layout and forms, including why twelve fields in three groups of four feel easier than one long list.

reads.title: Similarity Principle in Visual Design
reads.why: How shared colour, shape or size makes items read as related; note the advice to reserve your link colour for things that are actually clickable.

reads.title: The Principle of Common Region: Containers Create Groupings
reads.why: Why cards, panels and boxed sections work, and when a background or border is stronger than spacing alone; useful before you wrap everything in a card.
